lead: A `move` closure that reads only a `Copy` field of a drop guard captures the field, not the guard.
body: Since Rust 2021 a closure captures the most precise place it names, so `move || use(held.0)` copies the `Value` out and drops `held` when the enclosing function returns, and its `Drop` releases the reference early. That was `Core\Socket::upgrade`'s method entry freeing its callable before the connection ran. Name the whole guard inside the body first (`let held = held;`), and assert the reference count in the test, because reading a freed object often still gives the right answer.
